A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete STP convergence study, numerical experiments, and Appendix A. Body text matches throughout; rendered pages differ only in the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original simulations comparing STP, RGF, and GLD on a 500-dimensional quadratic, using 50 trajectories per algorithm and reporting outcomes in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original quadratic-optimization simulations, with 50 trajectories per algorithm and empirical outcomes in Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the identical three-point selection procedure. Search-direction choices and step-size prescriptions are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same quadratic minimization task in Section 6. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: RGF and GLD remain the evaluated comparators against STP in Section 6 and Figures 1–3, with identical implementations described.

E3.justification: The dimension, zero initialization, search distributions, step sizes, and evaluation procedures are identical. Both evaluate gradient norms against iterations and elapsed time, plus the scaled best-iterate gradient norm.

E4.justification: The convergence-rate illustration in Figure 3 is unchanged. Neither version adds or removes ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both specify 50 trajectories per algorithm and retain identical trajectory plots. Seed information, confidence intervals, and significance tests are absent from both.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 are visually identical, and their accompanying convergence findings and STP/RGF/GLD performance comparisons are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–7, Theorems 1–7, supporting lemmas, and all derivations and proofs in Appendix A are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims concerning almost-sure and expected convergence for smooth, convex, and strongly convex objectives, including best- and final-iterate guarantees.

C2.justification: Applicability conditions and interpretations are unchanged, including Section 6's explanation linking similar STP/RGF performance to their theoretical complexity bounds. No limitations or qualifications are revised.

D1.justification: Section 6 provides identical implementation details and hyperparameters for all three algorithms. No hardware, software, code-access, or data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, novelty positioning, and comparisons with earlier convergence analyses are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 23 Jan 2025 to v3 dated 22 Mar 2025. Manuscript wording, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1, Figures 1–3, equations, captions, and page layout are identical. The updated arXiv stamp does not change the manuscript layout.

improvement.justification: The complete manuscript, including experimental evidence and appendix proofs, is unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp neither resolves a deficiency nor alters scientific or presentation quality.
